title: Thai red curry squash soup
equipment: Large pot or Dutch oven with lid

items: 1 small butternut squash (about 2½ lb), peeled, seeded and cut into 1-inch cubes (about 6 cups)
1 (13.5 oz) can coconut milk, well shaken
½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
3 Tbsp coconut milk (saved from the can)

steps: Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5–6 min, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 min.
Stir in the curry paste and cook 1 min, stirring, until fragrant and a shade darker.
Pour 3 Tbsp of the coconut milk into a small cup and save it for topping. Add the rest of the can, the squash, broth and salt to the pot.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn to medium-low, cover and simmer 20 min, until the squash mashes easily with a spoon.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender. If using a countertop blender, fill it no more than halfway, remove the center cap and cover the hole with a folded towel so steam can escape.
Stir in lime juice a little at a time, and salt, to taste. Thin with a splash of broth if it's too thick.
Ladle into bowls. Swirl in the saved coconut milk and top with cilantro and pepitas.
tips: Curry paste brands vary in heat. Start with 2 Tbsp. You can stir in more after blending and simmer 2 min.
Stir in 1 tsp fish sauce with the lime for a deeper, saltier flavor.
Pre-cut squash from the store saves 10 min of peeling and chopping. Use 2 (20 oz) packages, about 6 cups.
storage: Fridge up to 5 days or freezer up to 3 months, without toppings. Reheat in a pot over medium heat, stirring, until steaming. Coconut milk can separate, so stir well.
